title: hOla Verde
team: Andrea Cutroni, Carlos Román, Claudia Serment
description: Sustainable design strategies for a timber office building in Málaga — natural ventilation, shading and a platform-frame structure in natural materials.
body: hOla Verde develops sustainable design strategies for an office building in Málaga, prioritizing natural ventilation, shading systems and a green roof. Sun-path studies across summer and winter days informed the shading and massing strategy.
The structure uses a timber platform-frame system with cork insulation and bamboo and recycled-material plaster for interior finishes, designed in AutoCAD, Revit and Twinmotion.

sections.title: Passive Strategies
body: The building is cooled without machinery. Cross-ventilation runs through the plan at both levels and exhausts under the curved roof, while fixed louvres and a deep overhang keep the summer sun off the glazing. Sun-path sections across a summer and a winter day set how far that overhang had to reach.

scenes.title: Ventilation
scenes.caption: Cool air drawn in at both levels and warm air released along the curve of the roof.

scenes.title: Summer
scenes.caption: At 9:00, 12:00 and 18:00 the high sun is cut by the overhang and the louvred screen before it reaches the glass.

scenes.title: Winter
scenes.caption: At 10:00, 12:00 and 16:00 the lower sun passes under the same overhang and reaches deep into the plan.

sections.title: Construction Process
body: The building goes up in eight stages, from a ventilated foundation to a planted roof. Everything above the slab is timber: platform-frame walls storey by storey, joisted floors, and curved glulam ribs carrying the roof.

scenes.title: 01 — Foundation
scenes.caption: Strip footings with the ventilated cavity system laid between them, forming the void under the ground floor.

scenes.title: 02 — Ground Slab
scenes.caption: The slab cast over the cavity formers, closing the ventilated void.

scenes.title: 03 — Ground Floor Walls
scenes.caption: Platform-frame walls raised on the slab, with openings framed and the internal partitions set out.

scenes.title: 04 — First Floor Joists
scenes.caption: Timber joists spanning across the ground-floor walls, with the stair opening left clear.

scenes.title: 05 — First Floor Deck
scenes.caption: The deck closed over the joists, giving the platform the next storey is built from.

scenes.title: 06 — Upper Walls
scenes.caption: The second set of platform-frame walls raised, with the window openings framed.

scenes.title: 07 — Roof Ribs
scenes.caption: Curved glulam ribs set on the upper wall plate, overhanging on both sides to shade the façades.

scenes.title: 08 — Green Roof
scenes.caption: The planted roof completed over the curve, its overhang forming the shading eave.

sections.title: Platform-Frame Structure
body: The envelope resolved in detail. Timber studs at 90×150 mm every 60 cm carry 15 cm of TRADITERM cork between OSB panels, finished outside in lime mortar under photocatalytic paint and inside in recycled-material plasterboard, with a bamboo floor over cork insulation.

scenes.title: Wall to Foundation
scenes.caption: The frame landing on the strip footing — sole plate, anchor bolts and the ventilated cavity with its PVC aeration pipe below.

scenes.title: Wall Build-Up
scenes.caption: The wall in plan: cork between the studs, OSB either side, and a 3 cm service void behind the interior finish.

scenes.title: Floor to Wall
scenes.caption: The floor meeting the frame — 10×20 cm joists on a steel angle, cork insulation and a bamboo finish over self-levelling screed.

sections.title: Views
body: The building in Málaga: a white volume under a planted curve, with louvred screens and a bamboo hedge along the shaded side.

scenes.title: Garden
scenes.caption: The shaded side across the garden, with the pergola, the water channel and the planting spilling off the roof.

scenes.title: Street
scenes.caption: The entrance front from the street, louvres closed against the afternoon sun.

scenes.title: Upper Floor
scenes.caption: Inside the open office level, under the exposed curve of the glulam ribs.
